handbookNote: Source: official New Mexico Driver Manual, published by the New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division (MVD, part of the Taxation and Revenue Department) and downloaded directly from realfile.tax.newmexico.gov/English%20Drivers%20Manualver11.19.19.pdf (file dated ver 11.19.19, i.e. the 11/19/2019 revision), linked from MVD's own official page mvd.newmexico.gov/mvd-drivers-license-manuals/. Full text extracted with pdftotext and saved to temp/handbooks/nm/driver.txt (a new file, distinct from the existing nm notary-track handbook file in that same folder). Every question in this bank is grounded in specific statements from that 40-page handbook text -- GDL permit/provisional/unrestricted rules, seatbelt/child-restraint law, traffic signals, traffic signs and pavement markings (incl. New Mexico's specific railroad-crossing and no-passing rules), other lane controls, general lane/turning rules, right-of-way (incl. the New Mexico White Cane Law, 28-7-1 NMSA 1978, and school-bus/emergency-vehicle rules), speed limits, parking (incl. New Mexico's specific no-parking distances and curb-color code), traffic violation points, basic driving/scanning/headlight-use technique, sight-distance and following-distance rules (3-second/4-second/10-second rules), communicating with other drivers, road conditions and New Mexico-specific wildlife-hazard content (deer/elk/antelope/bear/cougar by region), adjusting to traffic flow, bicycles and sharrows, large trucks/RVs, fitness to drive (vision/fatigue/health conditions/emotions/cell phones), DUI/DWI and drug law (incl. New Mexico's .08%/.02%-under-21 BAC thresholds and 25-year DWI record retention), vehicle emergencies and collision avoidance/skid recovery, collision protection and the Financial Responsibility Law's specific insurance minimums, and a notably deep New Mexico motorcycle-operation section -- no invented facts and no generic 'common knowledge' padding. Exam mechanics: the real per-item question count and whether the knowledge test is timed are NOT published anywhere in official New Mexico sources despite thorough research (the driver manual itself, the MVD's Driver Procedures Manual chapters 1-3, 5, 9, and 11, the MVD's Frequently Asked Questions page, and the Apply-for-a-Learner's-Permit / Drivers-Educational-Info pages all describe the 'MVD Knowledge Exam' requirement but never state a specific item count or a time limit) -- these are intentionally left UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed or reused from another state. The one exam-mechanics figure that IS officially published and CONFIRMED: the MVD's own Driver Procedures Manual, Chapter 11 ('Road And Written Test Requirements'), Section E ('Written Test Requirements', revised 12/08/2017), published at mvd.newmexico.gov/chapter-11-road-and-written-test-requirements/, states verbatim 'All class D and M written test scores must be 70% or better to pass.' Content depth: the manual's substantive body (about 40 pages after the table of contents) honestly supports this pool's depth and topic spread -- it is comparable to other states' driver handbooks in its core traffic-law coverage, and is unusually rich in New Mexico-specific motorcycle-operation guidance (braking technique, lane positioning, group riding formations, blind intersections, wobble recovery) and wildlife-hazard content specific to New Mexico's terrain and game animals; a few sections (e.g. traffic violations/points, speed limits) are comparatively thin in the source material, so those topic buckets were kept intentionally small rather than padded with invented or repetitive questions.
